topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url forms and derivation of joined URLs, authority, Host, and connection target
questions: May the base URL contain user-info, a path, query, fragment, percent escapes, an IPv6 zone, or multiple trailing slashes, and exactly how are authority, Host, connection target and joined URL derived from those forms?
Are user information, query, fragment and base-path components allowed in `api_base_url`; how many trailing slashes are removed; and exactly which textual authority becomes the Host header?
May api_base_url contain user information, a query, fragment, or non-root path, and does “without a trailing /” remove one slash or all trailing slashes?

judgement.why: This asks the same api_base_url, authority, Host and path-joining question as P13, and the reopening change did not touch any relevant passage.

precedent.topic: Valid api_base_url forms, Host authority, and path joining
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

topics.topic: Classification of addresses and hostnames for the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: How are IPv4, IPv6, mapped addresses, zone identifiers and hostnames such as `localhost` classified for the loopback exception?
Does loopback mean only a literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback address in the URL, or also a hostname that resolves to loopback, and how are mixed DNS results handled?
Does the exception require a literal loopback IP address, or may a hostname such as localhost qualify after DNS resolution?

quotes:
17. **Request body and addresses.** A JSON request body is sent as its RFC 8785
    canonical bytes. "Loopback" (A09 rule 4) is an IP literal in
    `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`; no name is resolved to decide it.
judgement.why: The later contract defines loopback as a literal IPv4 address in 127.0.0.0/8 or the IPv6 literal ::1 and excludes DNS resolution.

topics.topic: Detection and refusal ordering for duplicate JSON object members
questions: Are duplicate object member names in the installation or manifest refused, and if so at what check in each operation's first-failure order?
How can this operation detect duplicate object keys after its input has already become a JSON value, and which layer must perform that check?
Are duplicate object member names in a manifest record invalid, and if so at which manifest check are they reported?
Are duplicate object member names in the installation file invalid, including duplicates of scalar fields such as owner_token or manifest_revision?

judgement.why: Duplicate-member handling is a JSON parsing and validation-format contract, and its placement in first-failure order is also a State 6 concern.

topics.topic: Filesystem ownership, permissions, file types, and symlink checks at store startup
questions: What file types, owner and mode are accepted for the data directory and existing store entries, and does the symlink check recursively cover unknown entries as well as the database, value and spool areas?
What exactly makes the data directory and its existing contents private, and does `no symbolic link anywhere` cover path components, every recursive entry, database side files and unknown files?
What exact ownership and permission checks define a private data directory and private existing contents?

judgement.why: This is the same store ownership, permissions and recursive symlink-check question as P4, and the reopening change did not touch the relevant text.

precedent.topic: Privacy requirements for the store data directory and its contents
quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.

open_store: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError whose reason names the failed check: data_directory does not exist (it is never created here), lock held by another process, directory not private (naming the first offending path), or symbolic link found (naming its path); it removes and creates nothing when a check fails.
precedent.why: The later notes define privacy by effective-user ownership and no permissions for group or others across the directory and all contents, with a separate no-symlink traversal check.

topics.topic: Immutable resolution and reading of files at manifest_revision
questions: Is `manifest_location` an already materialized immutable tree, a repository read through a specific revision-aware mechanism, or a working tree whose current files are trusted, and what failures result when the revision cannot be resolved?
How is a file read at `manifest_revision`: from a checked-out immutable directory, through repository object access, or by changing/checking out the working tree?
How does bindings obtain the file at manifest_revision: from a Git object, a revision-named snapshot directory, or an already checked-out tree whose revision is merely asserted?

judgement.why: This is the same manifest-revision resolution and immutable reading question as P5, and the reopening change did not touch it.

precedent.topic: Resolution and reading of a configured manifest revision
quotes:
8. **The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
`<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
(A08 rules 1 and 6).
precedent.why: The later contract requires reading the manifest record as a Git object at the configured commit, never from the working tree.

topics.topic: Startup validation scope and ordering for installed service records and capabilities
questions: Which portions of a service record and which capability entries are validated at startup, in what order, before required-header collision checks?

Which A08 rule 5 checks count as checks of the record itself during startup, which capabilities are examined, and in what order, given that several checks require proposal ports or a particular operation?
Which A08 rule 5 checks are “of the record itself” at startup, when no operation name or proposed ports are available?

judgement.why: This is the same startup manifest-validation scope and ordering question as P9, and the reopening change did not affect it.

precedent.topic: Manifest validation rules applied to installed instances at startup
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Length unit and measurement point for masked failure details
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
Is the reported length a Unicode code-point count, UTF-8 byte count before truncation, or UTF-8 byte count of the retained bounded detail?

judgement.why: This is the same masked failure-detail length-unit question as P6, and the reopening change did not touch it.

precedent.topic: Unit and stage used to calculate masked failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later notes specify the masked length as the UTF-8 byte length of the stored failure_detail.

topics.topic: Persistence and return location of machine-readable operation failure detail codes
questions: Where is the machine-readable detail code stored and returned, and how is it distinguished from human-readable `failure_detail`?
Where is the closed operation_failed detail code persisted and returned when a response body also supplies failure_detail?

quotes:
11. **A NodeExecution and a TrialExecution carry `detail_code`** beside `failure_detail`: the closed
    detail of State 5 is a code, the excerpt is text, and the owner acts on the
    code.

send_under_authority: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The NodeExecutionDraft has status the SendResult outcome name (= models.NodeExecutionStatus), detail_code and failure_detail from the SendResult, executed the ExecutedBinding of the binding, inputs the element's input PortRefs, outputs one StoredValuesRef or SpooledFilesRef per output port in port name order, a SpooledFilesRef with the class the binding declares for that port, and no resources_used.

operation_element_conclusion: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns one ElementConclusion variant: ElementSucceeded with output PortRefs, ElementFailed with status and detail_code, ElementWaiting with reason (= models.WaitReason) and approval_id only for owner_approval, or ElementNotReached; a failed read propagates as an internal error and nothing is refused.
judgement.why: The later texts add a separate machine-readable detail_code to NodeExecution, persist it beside failure_detail, and return it on ElementFailed.

topics.topic: Representation of authored file inputs and expected outputs in trial cases
questions: How are bytes supplied for authored file inputs and expected file outputs, including `many` file ports, and which accompanying facts are caller-supplied versus kernel-computed?
How are authored file inputs and expected file outputs supplied, including their bytes, digest, size, media type and ordering for `many` ports?

judgement.why: This is the same authored trial-file representation and persistence question as P10, and the reopening change did not touch it.

precedent.topic: Representation of authored file fixtures for validation and byte persistence
quotes:
A value in a request is JSON text in a string field and a file is base64
   text, so that `surface` sees the exact text it canonicalizes, duplicate
   member names included; an answer carries values as JSON text and file bytes
   as base64.

handle_add_trial_case: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST turn each RequestPayload into a PortPayload of the same port: RequestJsonValue to JsonPayload with the canonical JSON bytes, RequestFile to FilePayload with the base64-decoded bytes, RequestFileList to FileListPayload with each element decoded, in list order; expected_outputs absent stays absent.

add_trial_case: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] Each input value becomes a StoredValue with the stored schema of its port (M21: the port's value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items) and the class its contract input port declares, each expected output a StoredValue with its port's stored schema and the highest class of the case's inputs from highest_disclosure_class; value_digest is content_identity of the bytes, value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent, and the bytes are stored with put_value_bytes; a port refers to its values by a StoredValuesRef, one value_id per file in list order for a many file port.
precedent.why: The later contracts make request files base64 text, convert them to byte-bearing FilePayload values, and persist those bytes after validation.

topics.topic: Required HTTPS trust roots and TLS verification policy
questions: Which trust store and TLS verification policy must `send_prepared_request` use so different HTTP clients do not accept different services?
Which trust roots, hostname rules and client TLS settings define successful verification?

quotes: TLS is verified for `https`.

No redirect, proxy or retry; `Accept-Encoding: identity`; TLS by instance
class; response limits; transport deadline (A09).

send_prepared_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] Sends the request exactly once to the URL host and port, never to the host header value; for https it verifies TLS with the URL host as the server name; it follows no redirect, ignores every proxy environment variable and retries nothing.
judgement.divergence: One implementer uses the host operating system's current trust store and default TLS policy, while another uses a release-pinned CA bundle and protocol/cipher policy; the owner and called service observe different connection successes and failures for the same certificate chain and TLS configuration.
judgement.why: The texts require certificate verification and fix the server name, but leave trust roots and the remaining TLS acceptance policy open.

topics.topic: Selecting the identity projection and list-sorting profile for content hashing
questions: How does the caller identify the hashing profile so that record-specific sorting is applied to contract or flow content, while manifest entries, request descriptions, idempotency inputs and ordinary list values preserve their semantic order?

How does the operation know which identity projection and list-sorting policy to apply when callers also use it for a manifest capability entry, request description, corpus list and idempotency-key material, none of which is a State 1 content record?

quotes: content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For every content variant of IdentitySubject (contract_version, implementation, trial_case, flow_version, stored_value, corpus) MUST build one JSON object whose members are exactly the variant's fields keyed by field name, subject_kind included, with nested models as objects keyed by field name, tuples as arrays, enum members as their value text, None as null and JSON-text fields such as value_schema kept as JSON strings, take its canonical bytes with canonical_bytes and return the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of those bytes.

content_identity: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Before hashing, lists whose order carries no meaning MUST be sorted so that the same content in another order has the same identity: ports by (direction, name), flow nodes by node_id, flow edges by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port), flow constants by (to_node, to_port), all compared as text by Unicode code point; every other list keeps its order, in particular trial_case_ids of a corpus (corpus order is meaningful) and the elements of any JSON value.

content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the idempotency_key variant MUST build one JSON object with one member per entry of fields, named by the entry's port and holding the JSON value its canonical_json encodes, so the order of the fields does not change the key, and return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of its canonical bytes; a field whose value is null is kept as null, not dropped.

content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the json_text variant MUST return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of json_text, and for the bytes variant the hexadecimal SHA-256 of content exactly as given, without any canonicalization; this is the digest of a file and of a value's bytes.
judgement.why: The later notes define tagged IdentitySubject variants, their exact projections, and the sorting rule for each kind of identity.

topics.topic: Validation and refusal ordering for flow and binding schemas
questions: Must binding port schemas be validated against the supported JSON Schema subset, and where does that check occur in A08's first-failure order?
Which schemas in a flow composition are subset-validated, and where does each validation fall in the pre-proof refusal order?
Which operation rejects an unsupported schema on a flow port, flow constant or binding port, with which refusal and at what position in its check order?

quotes:
2. **Supported JSON Schema subset** (A02 rule 1, carried by States 1 and 2): a
   schema is a JSON object using only `type` (one of `null`, `boolean`,
   `integer`, `number`, `string`, `array`, `object`, as one string), `enum`
   (a non-empty array of distinct scalars), `const` (one scalar), `properties`
   and `required` (for `object`), `additionalProperties` (`true` or `false`
   only), `items` (one schema, for `array`), `minItems`, `maxItems`,
   `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum` and `maximum`. Any other keyword —
   `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not` among them —
   is outside the subset: A02 refuses it in a contract version, and
   `fit_port_value` answers that no value fits it, so a binding or flow port
   written outside the subset can never deliver. `integer` means a canonical
   number without a fraction. A closed set (A05 guards) is a schema with `enum`
   or `const`. A `file` port's `value_schema` is the empty schema `{}`; its fit
   is its media type (State 5, `fit_port_value`).
judgement.why: State 6 deliberately refuses unsupported schemas only for contract versions; binding and flow ports may contain them, but fit_port_value ensures they can never deliver a value.

topics.topic: Byte representation used to measure JSON port-value size
questions: For a JSON value, is size measured from its RFC 8785 canonical bytes, the bytes originally received, or another representation?

topics.topic: Canonical structure hashed for multi-field idempotency keys
questions: What JSON structure is hashed for multiple key fields: an object keyed by field name, an array in manifest order, or a single scalar when there is one field?

topics.topic: Capabilities and observability of monotonic deadlines
questions: What exact capability is returned for checking expiry, and may callers read or compare the raw monotonic value?

topics.topic: Completeness of model records returned by read operations
questions: Do read operations return the complete stored model records, including identities, ownership links, actors and timestamps, or only the fields individually listed in each operation's Outputs section?

topics.topic: Credential newline stripping and control-character classification
questions: Does one trailing newline mean LF only or CRLF as one newline, and which Unicode characters count as control characters?

topics.topic: Exact sandbox exception text recorded as failure_detail
questions: What exact text is recorded for an exception, including qualification of the type, separator, empty messages and nested exception chains?

topics.topic: File information and bytes disclosed during effect approval
questions: Does an approval response show the owner the actual file bytes, or only their digest, size, media type and separately readable spool identity?

topics.topic: HTTP response grammar and framing violations classified as malformed
questions: Which HTTP grammar violations, duplicate headers other than Content-Type, obsolete folding and conflicting framing headers make a response malformed?

topics.topic: Handling of content-address and computed-identity collisions
questions: What does the store do on a detected content-hash collision for bytes, StoredValues or other content-derived records?

topics.topic: Handling of incompatible or corrupt existing store databases
questions: How does startup handle an existing database whose schema or integrity does not match this release?

topics.topic: Indexing convention for mapped element identities
questions: What map_index is assigned to the first and subsequent elements of a mapped node?

topics.topic: MCP transport, protocol version, and token carriage
questions: Which MCP transport and protocol version does the listener implement, and where in each request is the required owner or agent token carried?

topics.topic: Meaning, allowed forms, and enforcement of file-port value_schema
questions: What does `value_schema` mean for a file port, which schemas are valid there, and is it used only for proof-time equality or also for runtime validation of file metadata?

topics.topic: Persistence and return of TrialExecution failure_detail
questions: Does a TrialExecution persist and return bounded `failure_detail`; if so, in what field and for which outcomes?

topics.topic: Placement and encoding rules for multipart Content-Disposition port names
questions: Which port names are placeable in multipart headers, and are special characters escaped, encoded or rejected as `input_not_placeable`?

topics.topic: Position assignment for records created by multi-record changes
questions: In what order are positions assigned to every record created by each multi-record change, including StoredValues, Slot plus ContractVersion, AdmissionVerdict plus Activation, and attempt outcomes?

topics.topic: Processes and events counted toward sandbox process_count
questions: Does process_count include the initial Python runner, only child processes, or every process visible under the sandbox UID, and what exact event counts as hitting the limit?

topics.topic: Record-change identity, link, and lifecycle validation and error classification
questions: What exact identities and links must each named change validate, which lifecycle-field transitions are structurally allowed, and which violations return `refused` versus `internal_error`?

topics.topic: Safe failure_detail generation for transport failures without response bodies
questions: For transport failures with no usable response body, is `failure_detail` absent or synthesized, and if synthesized, what information is allowed so that paths, credentials and library-specific exception text cannot leak?

topics.topic: Sandbox outcome for values not representable as canonical JSON
questions: What sandbox outcome is produced when run returns a value such as NaN, infinity, a set, or another object that cannot be represented as canonical JSON?

topics.topic: Sandboxed agent access to runtime files and the exchange directory
questions: May agent code itself read arbitrary runtime files and create arbitrary files in the exchange directory, or are those paths available only to the sandbox runner for input/output transfer?

topics.topic: Schema requirements for inputs used as path placeholders
questions: Must a path-placeholder input also have value carriage and cardinality one, or may a file or many port pass proposal checks and fail every invocation as input_not_placeable?

topics.topic: Scope of bounded_text_bytes_max within nested JSON and schemas
questions: Does bounded_text_bytes_max apply to strings nested inside JSON values and schemas, or only to standalone textual fields such as names and purposes?

topics.topic: Stable formatting of refusal reason text
questions: What exact, stable reason text must each refusal return, including how fields and record identities are rendered?

topics.topic: Total ordering of otherwise equivalent flow edges and constants
questions: What total ordering is used when two edges have the same endpoints but different guards, or two constants target the same port, before proof later refuses or accepts them?

topics.topic: Translation of low-level store invariant and digest-mismatch refusals
questions: How must callers translate an ordinal-invariant refusal or a `put_value_bytes` digest mismatch: propagate `refused`, convert it to `internal_error`, or handle it as a normal domain result?

topics.topic: Unknown-reference versus relationship-mismatch handling in captured trial cases
questions: Which missing inputs produce `unknown_reference`, in what order, and which relationship mismatches instead produce `refused`?

topics.topic: Whether alternate resolved-address connection attempts count as retries
questions: May the HTTP client try another resolved address after a connection failure before any request byte is written, or does that count as a forbidden retry?

topics.topic: Whether request-level internal_error terminates the process
questions: Does every request-level `internal_error` terminate the process after responding, or only `stop_required`?

topics.topic: Wire representation counted by surface_request_bytes_max
questions: Which bytes count toward surface_request_bytes_max: the MCP payload, its serialized JSON-RPC envelope, or transport framing as well?

topics.topic: stop_required behavior after sandbox cleanup failure
questions: Can each of these operations return `stop_required`, after which committed decision, resumption and trace records remain and the process stops?
